facts.text: South Cairo was founded in 1803 as part of the Town of Cairo, originally called Canton, carved from Coxsackie, Freehold, and Catskill.
James Barker’s 1765 purchase of 6,000 acres along Catskill Creek sparked the first organized European settlement near what would become South Cairo.
In 1885 the Catskill Mountain Railroad extended a branch to Cairo, enabling timber, bluestone, hay, and fruit to reach Catskill Landing and spurring local mill development.
South Cairo sits along Catskill Creek, a major Hudson River tributary, and lies roughly 6.3 miles northwest of the village of Catskill.
The area’s wetlands and floodplains along Catskill Creek and Shingle Kill recharge aquifers and provide flood control, though seasonal flooding remains a risk.
Before European arrival, the Mahican people used the South Cairo landscape seasonally for fishing and as a trade route between the Hudson and Delaware valleys.
